Subject: MSA redline: narrow trade-secret/confidentiality exclusion + forensics protocol

Sally — attaching our redline of the MSA (CypherText_MSA_redline.docx) focused on the liability section. Two quick asks so procurement can move fast: 

1) We need a narrowly tailored exception to the liability cap for damages resulting from a proven confidentiality breach involving trade secrets (e.g., willful misappropriation). Our intent is to make this exception precise so it is not an open-ended carve-out.

2) We want to standardize a forensics/incident-evidence path so both parties agree who can perform forensics, timelines, and cost allocation if an investigation is required. See the attached redwood-forensics-protocol.pdf for our proposed vendor and process.

High-level proposal (inlined here for quick review):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in Section X (Limitation of Liability), Customer shall not be limited in its recovery of direct damages to the extent such damages arise from a Confidentiality Breach consisting of the willful and knowing misappropriation of Customer's Trade Secrets, provided that (i) Customer provides written notice within thirty (30) days of discovery; (ii) the party seeking damages obtains a written forensic report from an agreed independent forensic vendor confirming misappropriation by clear and convincing evidence; and (iii) the aggrieved party has complied with the preservation and mitigation obligations set forth in Section Y."

Notes: we intentionally kept the exception tied to "willful and knowing misappropriation" and required an independent forensic report to prevent speculative claims. Also proposed the 30-day notice window to keep investigations timely.

Can you confirm whether CypherText can accept the approach in principle? If so, Laura (CC'd) from Legal will follow with a refined clause that incorporates Redwood's preservation obligations and cost allocation mechanics.

Next steps we propose: procurement review + one quick call (30 min) to walk through the forensic steps. Timelines: we are hoping to finalize order form terms by EOW to keep the implementation start on track.

Thanks —

Markus — thanks for the redline and the clear proposal. A few initial reactions from our side: 

- We understand the need for a narrow carve-out. Our legal team is cautious about an exception that could swallow the cap; we would prefer the scope to be tightly limited to direct damages resulting from proven misappropriation of trade secrets.
- We can't accept open-ended costs for forensics. Can you confirm whether Redwood would cover initial forensics up to a reasonable cap? If not, we will insist on cost-shifting to the prevailing party.
- "Clear and convincing evidence" is a high bar; our counsel suggests tying the exception to "willful misappropriation as confirmed by an independent forensic report" but leaving evidentiary standards to the forum.

Proposed counter language (high level): "An exception to the liability cap will apply only to direct damages that are a direct result of an adjudicated or independently-forensically-confirmed willful misappropriation of Customer Trade Secrets; consequential and indirect damages remain excluded."

We also need to vet the named forensic vendors in your protocol. Can you share the vendor contact/credentials? Tom from Procurement (CC) will coordinate pricing and PO timing if we can land this approach.

Sally Tan

Sally / Team — Laura (Redwood Legal). Appreciate the quick read. I'm sharing a suggested, defensible clause below that limits exposure while addressing CypherText's concerns about cost allocation. Key points: (i) keep the exception strictly limited to direct damages from willful and knowing misappropriation; (ii) require independent forensic confirmation; (iii) Redwood offers to fund the initial forensic engagement up to $20,000 where there is a plausible basis for the claim; (iv) if the forensic report confirms misappropriation, Redwood will be responsible for the forensic costs; if not, Customer will bear the costs.

Suggested clause (redline-ready):
"Notwithstanding Section X, neither party's liability shall exceed the Liability Cap, except that Customer may recover direct damages in excess of the Liability Cap solely to the extent such damages are the direct result of the willful and knowing misappropriation of Customer's Trade Secrets by Redwood, provided that (A) Customer provides written notice to Redwood within thirty (30) days of discovery; (B) Customer commissions an independent forensic investigation from a mutually agreed vendor and provides Redwood with the resulting written report; and (C) the independent report concludes that, by a preponderance of the evidence, Redwood engaged in willful and knowing misappropriation. The party that does not prevail in the independent forensic determination shall reimburse the other party for the forensic costs, provided that Redwood will cover the initial forensic engagement costs up to $20,000 pending a reasonable basis for the investigation."

Additional operational points to add to the protocol:
- Evidence preservation checklist (preserve logs, access records, relevant S3 objects).
- 14-day window to grant vendor-scoped access after notice, subject to redactions for unrelated customer data.
- Escalation path and confidentiality protections for investigative materials.

I'll attach a tracked version back into the CypherText_MSA_redline.docx and include the forensics protocol with vendor references. If CypherText accepts the mechanics, procurement can proceed and Legal will coordinate the exact wording for the Order Form.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
